application_contracts.title: Compactness, ultrafilter and finite intersection
application_contracts.source_locator: Stacks Tags 086J and 08ZY, exact HTML snapshots of 2026-11-05; Milne CFT v4.03, V Theorem 2.2 p.155, VIII Corollary 7.3 p.258; direct common-alphabet and finite-stage arguments in closure-batch-006 and closure-batch-007
application_contracts.objects_and_maps: At each odd stage F=K F_o F_e F_s; common labels are the image of Gal(F/K) in retained quadratic coordinates. Projection to the K-split even alphabet is onto by definition; projection to the full odd alphabet is onto by K intersection F_o=Q. One ultrafilter retains these diagrams and finite coefficient tables.

Actual labels give nonempty unit residue classes; CRT adds finite independent incidence conditions before Dirichlet. The final intersection uses finitely many sets in one ultrafilter.
application_contracts.conventions: K-splitting is an individual prime condition; coefficient filters and stationary zero tests are total-label conditions. Each projection is separately onto; product surjectivity is not used. Choose b and its finite budget, then an actual stage, then prime representatives. Existing nonabelian detector and trace realizations remain A067.
application_contracts.translation_justification: Use finite intersection after proving each stage possible; never infer simultaneous satisfiability from unrelated individual solutions.

application_contracts.objects_and_maps: At each odd stage F=K F_o F_e F_s; common labels are the image of Gal(F/K) in retained quadratic coordinates. Existing nonabelian detector and trace realizations remain A067.
application_contracts.translation_justification: Use finite intersection after proving each stage possible; never infer simultaneous satisfiability from unrelated individual solutions.

application_contracts.title: de Rham property and weights
application_contracts.source_locator: Scholze published 2013, Corollary 1.8 pp.5-6, Theorems 9.1 p.74 and 9.3 p.75, with published 2016 corrigendum; Brinon-Conrad 2009 Theorem 5.2.1 and Propositions 6.3.3,6.3.8; Milne AV v2.00, I Theorem 12.1(a)
application_contracts.objects_and_maps: Actual Tate representation of A over L′; descend de Rhamness to Q_l and pass to multiplicity summand r_l.
application_contracts.hypotheses_and_discharge: Smooth proper A, finite local extension; de Rham category closed under summands and finite-extension descent. Hodge multiplicities must be compatible with the B action.

application_contracts.translation_justification: Comparison supplies de Rhamness of the geometric representation; descent and Morita multiplicities are separate standard inputs. Hodge–Tate alone would not imply de Rham.
